Can fully automated labor meet the demand of a market?

How simple should my answer be?

Yes. I think it can.
I dunno, does anyone really know for sure? I would assume so though, yes.
The people who are better informed to give an answer are the employers and we can see them all rushing to automation for over a decade now...

If you're asking if all labor jobs could be automated, no, they simply can't. Despite what people would like to believe, it takes a good deal of intelligence and knowledge to diagnose and repair most kinds of technology.

I suppose if we standardized everything so that a robot labor force could just analyze whether or not an object conforms to specifications, it might get closer to being possible, but AI would need to be much, much, MUCH more advanced than it is today in order to perform certain jobs. If that were to happen, things would get very boring because of the extreme level of standardization required.

This is well written. It makes a good point for a discussion I often have on this subject. Automation does not replace everyone, it makes the creation of an item more efficient (hopefully). This results in a net need for labor to create something to be reduced. We have been living with this model since the start of the industrial age, but it seems that we keep having this conversation in society. Of course any change causes disruption, but it also opens opportunity for the freed up labor to do something bigger and better. Granted this isn't always the result, but at least the opportunity is created.

I think our perception of what jobs they can do it's slightly skewed. We already have these deep learning algorithms that can predict cancer way better than humans can and I'm pretty sure I read there working on doing it with lawyers.

That depends on what you mean by "labor". If you mean "repetitive factory jobs" then yes, probably. If you mean "every job requiring human labor" then no, but large portions of industry could be replaced.

Not EVERYTHING could be replaced but enough things could be replaced that jobs wont be a mandatory requirement in the future. We're simply going to technology ourselves out of jobs and have to find another way to support society. Whether people like it or not that's just what's going to have to happen. There's not going to be enough jobs to go around in the future once more things get replaced with machines. Go to your local walmart. You're lucky as hell to see 2 or 3 cashiers. Everything is self-checkout now. It's things like that. Most factories are already machine operated. Now if you include jobs like cashiers, we're all going to be without jobs. In the next 100 years society is going to undergo MASSIVE changes that we've never seen before and I just hope it goes smoothly.

In the forseeable future, no it can't. It takes a level of analytical, problem solving, flexibility, and innovation to maintain complex machines.

Sure one day we'll have full blown AI which will have all the skills of humans and more, but that's far enough off that I'm not counting it.

However, service jobs like fast food, super markets, and roles like those will be significantly reduced in the next 20 years by self service and automation.
